main_text.p: Sic ait Hizkijahu: Dies tribulationis & increpationis atque blasphemiae dies haec. Quoniam venerunt filij usque ad locum partus, & non est vis pariendi. Si forte audierit Dominus Deus tuus verba Rabsakis, quem misit rex Assur dominus eius ad blasphemandum Deum viuente, & arguendum verbis, quae audiuit Dominus Deus tuus: ob id tu leuabis orationem pro reliquijs adhuc exi stentibus. Venerunt itaq; servi regis Hizkijahu ad Iesaiā. Et dixit ad eos Iesaiahu: Sic dicetis domino vestro: Sic dixit Dominus: Noli timere propter verba ista quae audisti, quibus me blasphemauerunt pueri regis Assur. Ecce ego pono in eo spiritu, & audiet rumore, revertetur q; in terra sua: & ego faciā eum cadere per gladiū in terra sua. Reuersus autē Rapsake, invenit regem Assur oppugnantē Libnam: audivit enim quod profectus esset de Lachis. Et audiens de Thirhaka rege Aethiopiae a dicente, Egressus est ut pugnet cōtra te: audiens, inquā, misit nuncios ad Hizkijam, dicens: Sic dicetis ad Hizkijam regem Iehuda, dicentes: Non decipiat te Deus tuus, in quo tu cōfidis, dicens: Non tradetur Ierusalem in manum regis Assur. page.notes: Block-letter-free page. The text runs on from the previous page, so the first paragraph is marked cont="true". The mark "·" before "Quoniam" and small stray marks at the right edge near "audisti" and "Lachis" are not printed words and are left out. Doubtful readings: "gladiū" (the vowel may carry a macron or be plain u), "Raplake" printed as "Raplake" (kept as printed). Long s is written as s throughout; "Reuerfus" and "Egreffus" have long-s forms and are rendered as "Reversus" and "Egressus". "Iefaiahu", "Iesaiá" and "Ierufa / lem" are rendered as "Iesaiahu", "Iesaiā" and "Ierusalem". The text is one continuous paragraph on this page, and the line "audi uit" is joined to "audivit".
